items.title: Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2013
items.q: I did not vote for both George Bushes or Ronald Reagan

ctx.x: I mean we have a divided country. And I’ll give you an example. I was a visiting professor at University of Michigan last November during the election. And I was staying in a hotel and there was one elderly white woman who was a native of Ann Arbor, Michigan, but I think somewhat far away from the university it seems, or she really didn’t have a connection. And she was disabled, and we had a friendly interaction, and I © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -9-

was trying to help her with the chair and she said it was nice. And she was complaining about where she lived, that she was on the second floor. And I said well can’t you change with the person on the bottom floor so you don’t have to go up the steps. The next day after Barack Obama was elected president she just went into a tirade. “I didn’t vote for communism, I didn’t vote for socialism, I’m going to leave the country.” And you know I supported Barack Obama, but if Mitt Romney had been elected I wouldn’t have…
And there was talk about, when Obama went into office, would this herald the start of the post-racial society. And it has not looked like it.
